te: Education under SDG 4, and following the world situation
se: Meeting on Wednesday 1 April 2026. The committee followed work on education under Sustainable Development Goal 4, such as lifelong learning, vocational skills and reducing school drop-outs. Challenges remain, such as rules, modern resources and PISA results, and the committee stressed raising the quality of education. It also followed the Middle East, OECD progress, Thai–Chinese relations, free trade agreements (FTA) and the Pink Economy.
it: International situation, the OECD, FTAs and the Pink Economy

te: Thailand's energy reserves of 96 days, and evacuating Thais from risk areas
se: The Ministry of Energy reported that Thailand has enough oil in reserve for about 96 days. 3 cargoes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from Qatar could not be delivered because of force majeure around the Strait of Hormuz, so spot LNG was bought instead. The situation was still at the “green” level. Key measures include temporarily suspending fuel exports (except to Lao PDR and Myanmar), raising legal oil reserves, moving biodiesel from B5 to B7 for a time, and energy-saving campaigns. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported that Thais had been evacuated from Iran in 2 rounds, back-up plans were ready for Lebanon and Iraq through Türkiye, and Thailand keeps a neutral position, using diplomacy to protect the national interest and the safety of Thais.
it: Energy security amid the Middle East situation (Ministry of Energy)
Care for and evacuation of Thais in risk areas (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

te: Conflict in the Middle East escalates: care for Thais and evacuation plans
se: The committee followed the conflict in the Middle East, which escalated into war with effects across the region, including energy shipping routes. About 110,000 Thais in the region may be affected, about 250–300 of them in Iran. The Royal Thai Embassy in Tehran prepared to evacuate a first group of 100 people by road through the Iran–Türkiye border on 7 March 2026. Most of the about 60,000 Thai workers in Israel chose to keep working.
it: The conflict in the Middle East and care for Thais in the region

te: Tourism in Phang Nga and the Andaman airport, and Nipah virus screening at airports
se: The committee heard about tourism in Phang Nga, which focuses on wellness and family tourism. Most visitors come from Europe and Scandinavia and stay about 14–30 days; in 2024 tourism brought in more than 50,000 million baht. The planned Andaman airport in Khok Kloi Subdistrict, Takua Thung District, about 7,500 rai with an investment of more than 80,000 million baht, would serve the Andaman provinces. Problems include damaged roads in places and flooding at Khao Lak. The committee also heard about the Nipah virus surveillance and screening measures of Airports of Thailand and the international communicable disease control checkpoints for passengers from risk areas.
it: Tourism potential of Phang Nga and the Andaman airport project

te: Appointing an honorary adviser, and following the international situation
se: The committee approved appointing an honorary adviser and a secretary to the committee, and followed key international developments, such as the situation in the Middle East and politics in Myanmar after its election. As a neighbour sharing a border of more than 2,000 kilometres, Thailand should have flexible policies to protect its interests and peace along the border. The committee also considered a visit to the border area.
it: Appointing an honorary adviser and a secretary to the committee
International situation: the Middle East, and Myanmar after the election

te: The situation in Iran and the safety of Thais, and the OECD on public governance
se: A representative of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported on the unrest in Iran, which began with economic protests in Tehran at the end of December and spread to many cities. The ministry is following it closely through the Royal Thai Embassy in Tehran and has prepared an evacuation plan in advance. At the time about 190 Thais lived in Iran; all were safe and no one had asked to be evacuated. The committee also followed work on public governance for OECD membership with the Office of the Public Sector Development Commission (OPDC).
it: The situation in Iran, its effects and care for Thais (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

te: OECD: the Anti-Bribery Convention and the work of the NACC
se: The committee heard the Office of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC), the lead agency for the OECD Anti-Bribery Convention, which aims to raise standards against bribery in international trade and investment. Thailand submitted its letter of intent to join on 8 December 2025. The NACC set up a steering committee to bring Thai law into line with OECD standards. The OECD has assessed Thailand's legal framework and proposed 6 further improvements. The next steps are to speed up legal amendments and prepare for the technical review.

te: Progress on Thailand's bid to join the OECD
se: The committee was told that Thailand has completed the steps of expressing its intent and drawing up a work plan, and on 8 December 2025 submitted its Initial Memorandum, a self-assessment, to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). The next step is the technical review, in which about 34 Thai agencies, led by the Office of the National Economic and Social Development Council, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Office of the Council of State, must work with the OECD's 25 committees. This is expected to take about 3–5 years, assessing laws, policies and actual practice. The committee proposed active public communication so that people understand the benefits of OECD membership.
it: Progress on joining the OECD (Initial Memorandum filed on 8 December 2025 and the technical review stage)

te: Following Thailand's progress towards OECD membership
se: Meeting on Tuesday 17 November 2026 at 13.30 hrs, Meeting Room 202, floor 2, Parliament House; members may also join online. The agenda is to adopt the record of the previous meeting, No. 18, and to consider and follow the progress of Thailand's work towards OECD membership, as set out in the meeting notice. A summary will be added after the Senate publishes the meeting summary.
it: Considering and following the progress of Thailand's work towards OECD membership
